description: Coding-agent CLI adapter layer for the rauf loop runner (epic agent-agnostic). Lets a single loop iteration be driven by any supported agent CLI — claude (default, first-class), codex, gemini, copilot, cursor, and a config-driven generic-cli — via the committed LLMProvider seam, with detection/fail-fast, agent selection precedence, and a CLI surface. Additive: the claude path stays behaviorally unchanged (SC-2). Implements PRD v2 / tech-spec v2 across spec docs 00-07; acceptance gate is `pnpm gate`.

items.title: Extract process-group.ts; delegate claude-process.ts to it (behavior unchanged)
items.description:
Extract the shared spawn/timeout/kill/group machinery out of claude-process.ts so CliAgent (item 004) and the claude path share one implementation. Pure internal refactor — SC-2 demands claude behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

1. NEW packages/loop/src/process-group.ts exporting (03 §5.1): `GRACE_PERIOD_MS = 30_000`; `SpawnProcessGroupOptions` { timeoutMs; signal?; cwd?; env?; stdin?; onStdout? }; `ProcessGroupResult` { exitCode; stdout; stderr; timedOut; durationMs }; `spawnProcessGroup(cmd, args, options): Promise<Result<ProcessGroupResult>>`; `killTree(proc, signal)`.
2. Move the existing claude-process.ts behavior VERBATIM (03 §5.2): `detached: true`, stdio pipes, env-merge-only-when-supplied, synchronous-spawn try/catch → err(FILE_NOT_FOUND), async proc.on('error') → err(FILE_NOT_FOUND), single-`resolved` guard, SIGTERM→GRACE_PERIOD_MS→SIGKILL on the NEGATIVE pid (whole group), abort → group SIGTERM (incl. already-aborted), EPIPE-tolerant stdin write/end, exitCode = code ?? 1 on close.
3. Refactor claude-process.ts to delegate to spawnProcessGroup: keep building the claude argv and the StreamParser/reconstructedText logic, but feed line-splitting via the new `onStdout` hook and remove the inlined timeout/kill/abort/stdin plumbing. Import GRACE_PERIOD_MS and killTree from process-group.ts. `spawnClaude`'s public signature, SpawnClaudeOptions, SpawnClaudeResult, and behavior stay byte-for-byte identical.

No caller of spawnClaude changes (claude-cli.ts:14, index.ts:12 re-export).

items.title: CliAgent config-driven engine (providers/cli-agent.ts)
items.description:
The single config-driven engine backing every non-claude CLI adapter. Declares the 00 §3.2 config types (they live in THIS file) and the CliAgent class.

1. NEW packages/loop/src/providers/cli-agent.ts. Declare and export `PromptDelivery = "stdin"|"arg"|"file"`, `BuildArgsContext { model?; promptFile? }`, and `CliAgentConfig` { id; displayName; binary; buildArgs(ctx); promptDelivery; nonInteractive: string[]; modelFlag?(m); env?; parsesStream?: false } exactly per 00 §3.2.
2. `export class CliAgent implements LLMProvider` exposing ONLY `id`, `displayName`, `execute`, `validateCredentials` — NO `checkUsage`, NO `dispose` (load-bearing: the runner gates usage on checkUsage being defined). Constructor takes a CliAgentConfig.
3. execute(prompt, options) per 03 §4: build argv = [...buildArgs(ctx), ...nonInteractive, ...(options.model && config.modelFlag ? config.modelFlag(options.model) : [])]; for promptDelivery 'arg' append prompt LAST; 'stdin' pass prompt as spawnProcessGroup stdin; 'file' write the prompt to a temp file INSIDE the cwd/ROOT_DIRECTORY, set ctx.promptFile, pass no stdin, and unlink it in a `finally` on every exit path (REQ-SEC-01). Pass timeoutMs = options.timeoutMinutes*60*1000, signal = options.signal, env = (config.env||options.env ? { ...config.env, ...options.env } : undefined) — options.env merged OVER config.env. Delegate to spawnProcessGroup (item 002). Return ok(ExecutionResult) with stdout/stderr/exitCode/timedOut/durationMs carried through and reconstructedText/parsedSignal/progressEvents UNSET. Nonzero exit and timedOut are DATA (ok). Spawn failure propagates err(FILE_NOT_FOUND); temp-file write failure returns err(IO_ERROR) before spawn.
4. validateCredentials() returns ok(undefined) without spawning or probing PATH.
5. Export CliAgent (value) + the three config types from providers/index.ts and the package barrel.
6. NEW cli-agent.test.ts: mock ../process-group.js (vi.fn spawnProcessGroup) and assert recorded (cmd,args,opts) for arg/stdin/file delivery; model-flag present/absent; nonInteractive always present; argv order; timeoutMs/signal forwarding; plain-text result (telemetry unset); nonzero & timedOut as ok-data; spawn-failure as err; file delivery unlinks temp even on spawn error; absence of checkUsage and dispose.

items.title: Agent-selection resolver + `agent` alias normalization at load boundaries
items.description:
The loop-agent-selection charter contract: a pure precedence resolver and the additive `agent`→`provider` input-alias fold applied at the @rauf/core load boundaries.

1. NEW packages/loop/src/agent-selection.ts (04 §3):
 - `resolveAgentId(input: { itemProvider?; runProvider?; projectProvider?; globalProvider? }): string` — pure, total, never throws; left-to-right coalesce with a `pick` that trims and treats empty/whitespace as unset; falls through to DEFAULT_AGENT_ID. Must satisfy the precedence matrix rows 1-9 (item > run > project > global > default).
 - `normalizeAgentAlias<T extends { provider?: string; agent?: string }>(raw, onWarn?): Omit<T,'agent'> & { provider?: string }` — folds `agent`→`provider`; if BOTH present, `provider` wins and onWarn is called once; the output never contains an `agent` key; passes through untouched when no `agent` key.
 - Re-export DEFAULT_AGENT_ID and GENERIC_AGENT_ID from ./constants.js. Package barrel re-exports resolveAgentId + both constants.
2. Apply the alias fold BEFORE Zod validation at each load site (04 §3.3) in @rauf/core: the backlog item parse (BacklogItem.provider — first VERIFY the exact parse site in packages/core/src/backlog.ts per the 04 §3.3 WARNING), readMarkerFile (MarkerOptions.provider), and readToolConfig (the `defaultAgent`→`defaultProvider` one-line variant fold). Additive and non-breaking: no schema field added or renamed; keep packages/core free of any cli/web import (the pure helper imports nothing beyond an optional onWarn sink).
3. NEW agent-selection.test.ts: all 9 precedence rows including row-5 keystone (`{}` → equals imported DEFAULT_AGENT_ID, not a literal) and row-8 whitespace-skip; totality (non-empty string for a representative input sweep, never throws); the four normalizeAgentAlias cases including `{ provider, agent }` → provider-wins with onWarn called once.

items.title: Signal-token neutralization before detection (neutralizeForDetection)
items.description:
Generalize the RAUF_* signal-token defusing so a quoted/inline token in any agent's output cannot be mis-parsed as a real completion signal (REQ-SEC-02, SC-6).

1. EDIT packages/loop/src/signal-redactor.ts (05 §4.4): widen the module's `SIGNAL_TOKENS` to ['RAUF_DONE','RAUF_BLOCKED','RAUF_NEEDS_HUMAN','RAUF_REVIEW'] (the prior set omits RAUF_REVIEW). Keep `redactSignalTokens(text)` exactly as-is (unconditional, log-only) but operating on the widened set. Add `export function neutralizeForDetection(text: string): string`: split into lines; for each line, if its TRIMMED content is exactly a token OR starts with `<token>:` (the reason/json forms), leave the line UNTOUCHED (legitimate standalone final-line signal); otherwise replace every token occurrence on that line via `tok.replace('_','·')`. Rejoin with '\n'. This neutralizes only NON-signal-line occurrences and preserves a genuine final-line signal.
2. EDIT signal-redactor.test.ts (SC-6): inline/quoted token (e.g. `prefix RAUF_DONE suffix`, `"RAUF_DONE" in a comment`) → after neutralizeForDetection, parseSignal returns 'none'; a standalone final-line `RAUF_DONE` / `RAUF_BLOCKED:reason` / `RAUF_NEEDS_HUMAN:reason` / `RAUF_REVIEW:{...}` is preserved → parseSignal returns the real type; RAUF_REVIEW both inline-neutralized and final-line-preserved (proving the token set widened); multiple inline tokens on one line all neutralized; the existing redactSignalTokens tests stay green.

This item only adds the function + tests; wiring it into the runner's two parseSignal sites is item 010.
acceptanceCriteria: signal-redactor.ts SIGNAL_TOKENS includes RAUF_REVIEW and both redactSignalTokens and neutralizeForDetection use the widened set

pnpm gate passes
items.notes: parseSignal matches whole-line signals scanning backward, so line-awareness is the correct discriminator: a token sharing its line with other text is never a real signal. Keep redactSignalTokens (log-preview) and neutralizeForDetection (pre-detection) as two distinct functions.

items.title: Runner usage-gating + pre-loop fail-fast detection + neutralization sites
items.description:
Make the routed runner correct and safe for non-claude agents: gate all Anthropic usage handling, add pre-loop fail-fast detection, and apply signal neutralization at both detection sites. Builds on item 009.

EDIT packages/loop/src/runner.ts (05 §3.6, §3.7, §4.3, §4.5):
1. Usage gating (REQ-USAGE-01/02): gate ALL Anthropic usage handling on `provider.checkUsage` being defined (not on id===claude-cli). Resolve the run-level provider first; run the pre-loop usage preflight (runUsagePreflight) and the between-iterations usage check only when the run-level provider exposes checkUsage (its cancellation check stays UNgated). Wrap the mid-iteration pre-signal usage-banner scan (hasUsageLimitInText on stderr/signalText) inside `if (provider.checkUsage)`. For the post-signal classification, when the iteration provider has NO checkUsage, downgrade a `usage_limited` classification to `genuine_retry` so handleStderrUsageLimit (claude OAuth) is never called. classifyExit/ExitClass themselves stay unchanged.
2. Pre-loop fail-fast (REQ-DET-02, SC-3): add `detectAllCandidateAgents(pendingItems)` — candidate set = run-level resolved id + every distinct per-item provider among pending items; detectAgent each; on any unavailable return an AgentUnavailableError-shaped err({ code: FILE_NOT_FOUND, message naming the agent + 'Install it or ensure "<binary>" is on PATH' + 'Supported agents: <ids>' }). Add `failRunSetup(error)` returning the zero-iteration LoopResult ({ completedCount:0, blockedCount:0, cancelled:false }) after emitting loop_error. Call detection FIRST in run()'s try — BEFORE writeState('starting', null) and before the usage preflight — and early-return on failure with NO state written and NO fallback to claude.
3. Neutralization sites (REQ-SEC-02): apply `neutralizeForDetection` (item 008) immediately before parseSignal at BOTH sites — work iteration on signalText, review pass on raw stdout. Keep the existing redactSignalTokens log-preview use unchanged. Add neutralizeForDetection to runner.ts's import from ./signal-redactor.js.

EDIT runner.test.ts: a non-checkUsage provider whose stdout contains 'rate limit' is NOT classified usage_limited and raises no error; no preflight/OAuth read for a non-claude run-level provider; a checkUsage provider (claude fake) still runs the usage paths; fail-fast — detectAgent → { available:false } makes the runner return the AgentUnavailableError-shaped error before iteration 1 with the state-writer seam NOT invoked, no backlog status mutation, and the message naming agent + remediation + supported ids; neutralizeForDetection applied at both parseSignal sites.
acceptanceCriteria: Pre-loop preflight, between-iterations usage check, mid-iteration pre-signal banner scan, and post-signal usage_limited arm are all gated on provider.checkUsage (cancellation check NOT gated)

A non-claude (no checkUsage) agent printing 'rate limit'/'usage limit' in normal output is NOT classified usage_limited and raises no error; claude-cli still runs every usage path exactly as today (SC-2)

detectAllCandidateAgents probes the run-level id + every distinct per-item provider and returns an AgentUnavailableError-shaped error (FILE_NOT_FOUND) naming the agent + remediation + supported ids on any unavailable
Fail-fast runs before writeState('starting', null) and before the usage preflight; on failure NO state.json is written, NO backlog status mutates, and there is NO fallback to claude
neutralizeForDetection is applied immediately before parseSignal at both the work (signalText) and review (stdout) sites; the redactSignalTokens log-preview use is retained
runner.test.ts covers usage-gating skip (no spurious usage_limited), claude usage paths preserved, fail-fast with no-state-written, and both neutralization sites; pnpm gate passes
items.notes: The cleaner alternative for the post-signal arm: `const exitClass = provider.checkUsage ? classifyExit(...) : downgradeUsageLimited(classifyExit(...))` where downgradeUsageLimited maps usage_limited→genuine_retry. failRunSetup must return the committed zero-iteration LoopResult shape (runner.ts) — the contract is 'zero iterations, no state write', error surfaced via the loop_error event. Detection must run after the item-009 project/global reads.

items.title: CLI surface: --agent flag, --help enumeration, and `rauf agents` command
items.description:
The operator-facing CLI in packages/cli — additive, thin, no registry coupling beyond consuming the loop barrel exports.

1. EDIT packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts (06 §3-4):
 - In handleLoopRun, read `const agent = extractStringFlag(ctx.flags, "agent") ?? undefined;` (beside the existing model read) and add `provider: agent` to the LoopStartOptionsSchema.parse({...}) assembly. Omitting --agent must leave provider undefined (identical to today).
 - In runDetached, read `const agent = extractStringFlag(ctx.flags, "agent");` (string|null, NOT coalesced — distinct from the in-process `?? undefined` read above) and `if (agent !== null) body.provider = agent;` mirroring the existing body.model send.
 - Add exported `handleAgents(ctx): Promise<number>`: await listAgents() (catch defensively → error + ExitCode.ERROR); for --json (ctx.globalFlags.json) outputJson({ agents: rows }); else render a renderTable with columns ID/NAME/AVAILABLE/DETAIL where available is c.green('yes')/c.yellow('no') and detail is r.detail ?? ''. Return ExitCode.SUCCESS (0) even when all agents are unavailable; spawn no agent subprocess.
2. EDIT packages/cli/src/commands.ts (06 §3.2-3.3): import getAgentDescriptors from @rauf/loop; compute `const SUPPORTED_AGENT_IDS = getAgentDescriptors().map(d=>d.id).join(", ")` once at module load; add a `--agent <id>` FlagDef to the `loop run` flags array whose description enumerates SUPPORTED_AGENT_IDS and points to `rauf agents`; add a top-level `agents` CommandDef (name 'agents', usage 'rauf agents [--json]', a --json FlagDef, handler: handleAgents, no subcommands) plus the handleAgents import.
3. EDIT loop-commands.test.ts: `rauf loop run --agent codex` sets options.provider === 'codex' (in-process) and body.provider === 'codex' (detached); `rauf loop run --help` enumerates ids from getAgentDescriptors() (sync, no PATH probe); `rauf agents` lists each descriptor's id/displayName/available from listAgents() and --json emits { agents: [...] }; the llm_spawned/llm_exited formatter is unchanged.
4. EDIT packages/cli/src/commands.test.ts (06 §Verification): assert the `loop run` command's flags array contains a `--agent` FlagDef whose description enumerates SUPPORTED_AGENT_IDS, and that a top-level `agents` CommandDef (name 'agents', handler handleAgents, a --json FlagDef, no subcommands) is registered. This is the registration-side test, distinct from loop-commands.test.ts (behavior).
acceptanceCriteria: rauf loop run [path] --agent <id> sets options.provider (in-process) and body.provider (detached); omitting --agent leaves provider undefined
A --agent <id> FlagDef is registered on `loop run` with a description enumerating SUPPORTED_AGENT_IDS from getAgentDescriptors() (computed once at module load, synchronously)

`rauf agents` is a top-level command (handler handleAgents, no subcommands) printing an ID/NAME/AVAILABLE/DETAIL table from listAgents(), returning exit 0 even when agents are unavailable and spawning no subprocess
`rauf agents --json` emits { agents: AgentAvailability[] }
The llm_spawned/llm_exited formatter is unchanged (already prints event.provider)
commands.test.ts covers the --agent FlagDef registration on `loop run` and the `agents` CommandDef registration (06 §Verification)
loop-commands.test.ts covers --agent plumbing (both paths), --help enumeration, and the agents listing/--json; pnpm gate passes
items.notes: 06 §3.1.2 WARNING: confirm the web start route deserializes body.provider into LoopStartOptionsSchema before relying on the detached path (provider is a committed schema field, so it should). The CLI does NOT pre-validate the id against the registry — unknown/absent ids are surfaced by the runner's fail-fast/per-iteration resolve (items 009/010). getAgentDescriptors enumerates built-ins only (claude-cli + 4 presets + generic-cli) — depends on 005/006 having registered them.

items.title: Generalize test-sandbox harness + add plain-text mock agents
items.description:
Generalize the test-sandbox so a loop can be driven end-to-end through each mock agent, while keeping every existing claude scenario unchanged (SC-2). Bash only — no production code.

1. Add plain-text mock dispatchers alongside test-sandbox/claude (07 §4.2): test-sandbox/codex, test-sandbox/gemini, test-sandbox/copilot, and test-sandbox/cursor-agent (binary name is cursor-agent, matching the preset). Each is a tiny dispatcher (like claude) that resolves the scenario from MOCK_AGENT_SCENARIO (fallback MOCK_CLAUDE_SCENARIO, then stream-done) and execs the scenario script in PLAIN-TEXT mode (export MOCK_AGENT_FORMAT=plain).
2. Add test-sandbox/mock-generic-agent.sh — the target for the reserved generic-cli adapter, driven via a providerConfig ({ binary: <abs path>, promptDelivery: 'stdin', nonInteractive: ['--auto-approve'] }); emits plain text + a final-line RAUF_DONE.
3. EDIT test-sandbox/scenarios/*.sh to emit EITHER stream-json (claude) OR plain text, selected by MOCK_AGENT_FORMAT. Prefer a shared scenarios/_emit.sh helper (emit_done/emit_blocked/emit_needs_human branching on MOCK_AGENT_FORMAT) so the stream-json and plain-text forms carry the SAME signal on the final non-empty line. In plain mode emit no message_start/content_block_*/message_delta JSON (so no token/tool telemetry exists).
4. EDIT test-sandbox/claude dispatcher: resolve the scenario as MOCK_AGENT_SCENARIO first, falling back to MOCK_CLAUDE_SCENARIO then stream-done (so every existing MOCK_CLAUDE_SCENARIO usage keeps working).
5. EDIT test-sandbox/run.sh: add an agent selector + a `run_agent_scenario <agent> <scenario>` helper (the cross-agent sibling of run_scenario) that resets the sandbox, exports the scenario env, puts the chosen mock binary first on PATH, and runs `rauf loop run "$SANDBOX_DIR" --iterations 1 --timeout 1 --agent <id>`. For <agent>=claude (or no --agent) behavior is exactly today's path.

This item adds the harness + mocks; the per-agent assertions live in item 013.
acceptanceCriteria: test-sandbox/{codex,gemini,copilot,cursor-agent} and test-sandbox/mock-generic-agent.sh exist, drain stdin, emit plain text + a final-line RAUF_* signal, and emit no stream-json telemetry in plain mode
scenarios/*.sh emit stream-json (claude) or plain text selected by MOCK_AGENT_FORMAT, carrying the same signal in both forms
test-sandbox/claude resolves the scenario via MOCK_AGENT_SCENARIO with a MOCK_CLAUDE_SCENARIO fallback; existing MOCK_CLAUDE_SCENARIO usage is unchanged
run.sh exposes a run_agent_scenario helper that puts the chosen mock first on PATH and runs `rauf loop run ... --agent <id>`
Running an existing claude scenario via the generalized run.sh behaves exactly as before
pnpm gate passes (the unit suites are unaffected by the sandbox changes)
items.notes: The sandbox redirects git to a throwaway repo (GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE) so commits stay out of the parent repo. verify.sh is NOT part of pnpm gate — this item's gate is just the unit suites; the sandbox is validated by item 013 via `bash test-sandbox/verify.sh`. Reuse over duplication: one signal source of truth per scenario across both formats.

items.title: verify.sh per-agent + fail-fast + SC-2 regression assertions
items.description:
Add the cross-agent integration assertions to test-sandbox/verify.sh, proving SC-1/SC-3/SC-4 end-to-end and SC-2 regression. Builds on the harness from item 012.

EDIT test-sandbox/verify.sh (07 §4.3, §5, §6):
1. Add `assert_event_provider <id>`: jq over .rauf/events.ndjson asserting some llm_spawned/llm_exited event has provider == <id>, AND no llm_spawned/llm_exited event carries 'claude-cli' for a non-claude run.
2. For each of codex, gemini, copilot, cursor (via cursor-agent), and generic-cli (via providerConfig→mock-generic-agent.sh): run the stream-done scenario (plain mode) through run_agent_scenario and assert — item 001 done (assert_item_status), DONE file exists, state limit_reached, exactly one [rauf] 001: commit (assert_dogfood_commit), assert_event_provider <id>, NO 'Usage limit detected' line in .rauf/rauf.log (preflight skipped, REQ-USAGE-02), and NO token-count / llm_tool_activity events (telemetry gracefully absent), with no error.
3. Add one non-claude stream-blocked run (e.g. codex) asserting item 001 status 'blocked' (plain-text RAUF_BLOCKED parsing, REQ-SIG-02).
4. Add a fail-fast row: `rauf loop run "$SANDBOX_DIR" --iterations 1 --timeout 1 --agent codex` with NO codex mock on PATH, on a fresh sandbox — assert non-zero exit naming codex + how to install/PATH, assert_file_not_exists .rauf/state.json, item 001 still at its pre-run status (no backlog mutation), no [rauf] commit since baseline, and the output does NOT mention falling back to claude.
5. Confirm all existing claude scenarios (stream-done, stream-blocked, stream-tools, slow-stream, stream-needs-human, usage-limit-stdout, commit-no-signal, fast-infra-death, pause-resume-needs-human, multi-backlog/compat) still pass unchanged.

The deliverable is `bash test-sandbox/verify.sh` green across all rows (it is a manual integration check, not part of pnpm gate).
acceptanceCriteria: assert_event_provider <id> exists and asserts the real agent id in llm_spawned/llm_exited and the absence of 'claude-cli' for non-claude runs

Each of codex/gemini/copilot/cursor/generic-cli runs stream-done (plain) and asserts item 001 done + commit + provider==<id> + no 'Usage limit detected' log + no token/llm_tool_activity telemetry + no error
One non-claude stream-blocked run asserts item 001 'blocked' (plain-text RAUF_BLOCKED)
A fail-fast row (--agent codex, no codex on PATH, fresh sandbox) exits non-zero naming codex, writes no state.json, mutates no backlog status, makes no commit, and never mentions claude fallback
All existing claude scenarios still pass unchanged (SC-2)
bash test-sandbox/verify.sh is green across all rows, and pnpm gate passes
items.notes: Reuse the exact existing marker the usage-limit-stdout case greps for: `! grep -q "Usage limit detected" "$SANDBOX_DIR/.rauf/rauf.log"` as the no-preflight assertion. 'No state written' is concretely (a) no .rauf/state.json, (b) no backlog item status change, (c) no per-item commit.
